title: Marta bat Baitos the Earlier
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: She was very wealthy, as in the Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubot, end of chapter 5: the Sages decreed for her two se'ah of wine every day, and she was then nursing, and she cursed them: 'So may you give to your daughters.' And her wealth grew so great that she became a byword on everyone's lips, as in Ketubot 104a: Abaye said to Rav Yosef, 'And Marta daughter of Baitos — up to twenty-five years?'

And Hyman places her in the time of King Yannai son of Yohanan, the high priest, and Shimon ben Shetah was then president of the Sanhedrin. When she was a widow she became betrothed to Yehoshua ben Gamla, and she gave King Yannai tarkabs (measures) of dinars, and he installed Yehoshua ben Gamla as high priest; afterward she married him, as expressly stated in Yoma 18a and Yevamot 61a. This Yehoshua ben Gamla is remembered for good, as explained in his entry. She had a son (by Yehoshua ben Gamla) of great strength, as in Sukkah 52b: they said that the son of Marta daughter of Baitos would take two thighs of a large ox bought for a thousand silver pieces and walk heel to toe, etc. And there are

notes.text: The named Ketubot104a passage expressly says twenty-five years. Hyman’s historical placement of Marta and Yehoshua ben Gamla remains his account. The supplied notice ends with “And there are,” a transition whose continuation is not supplied here.

Three whole saved Davidson digital scalars were read with raw SHA256, exact selectors, scalar hashes and actual edition metadata checked: Yoma18a (259 chars), Sukkah52b (341 chars), and the legacy-schema Ketubot104a he[11] scalar (188 chars, including its original HTML markup). Ketubot explicitly says twenty-five years in Abaye's genuine question to full Rav Yosef; this supports the contextual numeral reading without Hebrew or printing-history repair. Hyman's Jerusalem Talmud end-of-Ketubot-chapter5 wine account, two se'ah every day, nursing and plural curse to the Sages are retained but not newly checked against a whole named Jerusalem Talmud passage. Hyman's placement under King Yannai son of Yohanan the high priest, Shimon ben Shetah's Sanhedrin presidency, widowhood, betrothal, subsequent marriage and parenthetical assignment of the son to Yehoshua ben Gamla remain his account, not newly admitted chronology, identity or genealogy. The whole Yoma scalar supports only the dinar-measure appointment report in its local context; it does not establish the full chronology or later marriage. Hyman's plural tarkabs (measures) is retained beside the digital singular tarkabba, with no inferred measure count or conversion. Yehoshua ben Gamla's supplied blessing is remembered for good, not a substituted of blessed memory. The Sukkah scalar describes her son's two ox thighs and heel-to-toe feat but does not name his father; it says a thousand zuz where Hyman supplies a thousand silver pieces. Both denominations remain distinct, without replacing the Hebrew or inferring paternity. Its preceding comparison and following priestly prohibition/scriptural rationale are not imported. Neither Yevamot61a nor the separate Yehoshua entry is newly verified. The heading's the Earlier renders הקדומה without establishing an age, date or identity with the next notice. The supplied source ends with ויש, And there are; no continuation or identity with the separately headed Marta/Miriam notice is invented. The older Yoma35b nonmatch remains a bounded historical observation, not global absence. All three original mixed notes, the current mixed note, all historical English, carried notes and original responses remain exact. The original request to revise the mixed note is not applied; this is an additive qualification. Source hold p003 is retained.

The complete consulted Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:11 passage states two se’ah of wine every day, discusses nursing, and gives the plural curse concerning the Sages’ daughters. It also contains a separate account about Miriam; the English commentator’s proposed identification of the women is not adopted here. Yevamot 61a expressly gives Marta’s betrothal, Yehoshua ben Gamla’s appointment, and their subsequent marriage. These passages do not establish Hyman’s full placement under Yannai son of Yohanan, Shimon ben Shetah’s role, or his parenthetical identification of the strong son’s father. Sukkah 52b calls him Marta’s son without naming his father and uses a thousand zuz beside Hyman’s thousand silver pieces. The printed volume III, p. 911, confirms that this notice ends with ויש, “And there are,” immediately before a separately headed notice, “Marta (or Miriam) daughter of Baitos,” about the siege. No continuation has been added to the supplied notice, and no identity between the separately presented women is inferred. The historical notes above are retained; the newly consulted witnesses supplement their earlier inspection limits.
